title: Explaining a Concept
description: A first-year student says: "Group work just means splitting the assignment into parts." Your group must explain to this student what makes group work truly collaborative, in clear everyday language.
promptForGroup: What is the difference between dividing work and learning together? What example from your own experience would make the difference clear?

title: Improving a Weak Answer
description: A student wrote: "Group work is useful because the work gets done faster when you split it up." Your group must discuss what is incomplete or misleading about this answer and how to improve it.
promptForGroup: What benefits of collaborative learning are missing? Are there situations where splitting the work actually reduces learning? Agree on how you would revise the answer.

title: Short Case Study
description: In a four-person project group, one student does almost nothing while another takes over every decision. The teacher is considering three changes: peer assessment of contributions, assigned roles (facilitator, recorder, critic, presenter), or a short individual quiz on the group's work. Analyse the trade-offs and recommend one approach.
promptForGroup: How would each option affect participation, fairness and learning? Who benefits and who might be harmed? What assumptions are you making?

title: Making a Judgment Call
description: A group project is due tomorrow. One member suggests asking an AI for a complete answer, submitting it, and "reading it properly later". Discuss whether this is acceptable and under what conditions using a full AI answer in group work could be justified.
promptForGroup: Weigh learning, honesty, fairness to the group and time pressure. What criteria should guide the group's decision?

title: Learning Activity – Understanding Different Types of Learning Regulation
description:
When students work individually or in groups, they use different strategies to manage their learning, overcome difficulties, and achieve their goals.

• Self-Regulated Learning (SRL): A student takes responsibility for their own learning by setting goals, monitoring their understanding, identifying difficulties, and adjusting their approach when necessary.

• Co-Regulated Learning (CoRL): One student helps another manage or improve their learning, for example, by providing guidance, asking questions, or helping them recognise mistakes.

• Socially Shared Regulation of Learning (SSRL): Group members work together to set common goals, monitor their collective progress, identify challenges, and adjust their strategies to achieve a shared learning outcome.
promptForGroup: Imagine a group of three students working together on a difficult assignment. Explain how Self-Regulated Learning (SRL), Co-Regulated Learning (CoRL), and Socially Shared Regulation of Learning (SSRL) could each occur during this activity. Provide one practical example of each and explain how these different approaches can contribute to successful collaborative learning.

title: Reflecting on Meaningful Participation
description: Visible activity, such as the number of messages sent or the amount of text written, does not always show how much a contribution helped the group learn.
promptForGroup: Does contributing more messages or writing more of the final answer necessarily mean that someone participated more meaningfully? Reflect on what makes a contribution valuable to group learning and explain how members can help each other develop a better understanding, even when they contribute different amounts.

title: Ethical Dilemma
description: An AI tool can write a group's project report in minutes, but some groups use it so that no member engages with the topic. Should your institution allow unrestricted AI use in group projects, restrict it, or ban it? Defend your group's position.
promptForGroup: Consider fairness, learning outcomes, each member's contribution and enforcement. Where do you draw the line between support and substitution?

title: Data Interpretation
description: Students studying in groups scored 12% higher than students studying alone. However, 45% of students in groups reported unfair workloads.
promptForGroup: Do these results prove that studying in groups leads to better learning? Answer Yes or No and briefly explain why.

title: Designing a Process
description: Four students must divide the work for a group presentation. Some students have more free time or experience than others.
promptForGroup: Is giving every student exactly one topic always a fair way to divide the work? Answer Yes or No, briefly explain why, and suggest one way to make the process fairer.

title: Synthesis and Recommendation
description: Think about how your group used AI assistance during the activities.
promptForGroup: Should groups always follow AI suggestions when completing an assignment? Answer Yes or No and briefly explain your answer. Suggest one good practice for using AI in group work.
